references.text: En-Gedi is mentioned as a place along the Dead Sea where fishermen will stand and cast their nets, a prophetic vision of restoration.
David stayed in the mountain strongholds of En-Gedi when he fled from Saul, showing the strategic importance of the place.
Saul pursued David to the wilderness of En-Gedi, where there were caves in which David hid.
En-Gedi is mentioned in the Song of Songs as a place known for its vineyards and henna bushes.
En-Gedi is identified with Hazazon-Tamar, where hostile armies gathered against King Jehoshaphat.
Hazazon-Tamar, which is En-Gedi, is mentioned in connection with the kings who waged war in the area.
